questions.question: What is a topic sentence?
options: A sentence that presents the main idea of a paragraph, usually placed first
The last sentence in an essay
Any sentence with more than ten words
questions.explanation: The topic sentence presents the main idea of the paragraph and usually comes first, so the reader knows what the paragraph is about.

questions.question: In the TEXAS paragraph model, what does the X stand for?
options: eXample - give an example or evidence
questions.explanation: TEXAS = Topic sentence, Explain, eXample, Analyse, Summary. The X reminds you to support your point with an example or evidence.

questions.question: How many main ideas should one paragraph have?
questions.explanation: A paragraph should develop ONE main idea. If you have several ideas, split them into separate paragraphs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of transition words like "however" and "in addition"?
options: To connect sentences and ideas so the text flows logically
To show that the text is finished
questions.explanation: Transition words bind sentences and paragraphs together and show the reader how the ideas are connected.

questions.question: A paragraph jumps between football, homework and holidays. What is the main problem?
options: It contains too many different ideas instead of developing one
It uses too many transition words
It has too many examples for one idea
questions.explanation: A common paragraph mistake is including too many ideas. All sentences in a paragraph should support the same main idea.
